newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Staff buy Chinese loss-making state enterprise.
newsitem.headline: Staff buy Chinese loss-making state enterprise.

text.p: The staff of China's loss-making state-run Chongqing Jialing Chemical Plant, which has assets totalling 150 million yuan, have taken over the firm, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Thursday.
This marked a new experiment in reforming China's medium- and small-sized state enterprises, the newspaper said.
The assets-to-liabilities ratio of Jialing Chemical, which employed 1,200 people, had reached 98 percent, it said.
The staff had undertaken all of the plant's liabilities, it said, but did not detail how the staff had done so or how much they had paid.
Jialing would become a collectively-owned enterprise and had been renamed Chongqing Jialing Chemical Products Co Ltd, the newspaper said, giving no other details.
China has vowed to breathe new life into its lumbering state sector which is burdened with heavy debt and weak management, a legacy of decades of central planning.
Beijing has been encouraging acquisitions and mergers among state enterprises but has so far largely avoided bankruptcy because of fears that massive layoffs could lead to social unrest.
